channel.title: Can I use sudo in daily use
channel.description:
| `user-sysmaint-split`: multiple boot modes for better security | Kicksecure increases safety by enforcing use of separate accounts for daily use and administrative tasks. This is called [user-sysmaint-split](https://www.kicksecure.com/wiki/Sysmaint "Sysmaint"). It prevents daily used, high-risk software with large attack surface that can be hacked such as a web [browser](https://www.kicksecure.com/wiki/Browser "Browser") from gaining full administrative ("[root](https://www.kicksecure.com/wiki/Root "Root")") access. Therefore, otherwise trivial deployment of rootkits and [firmware trojans](https://www.kicksecure.com/wiki/Backdoor#Firmware_Trojan "Backdoor") (a type of [malware](https://www.kicksecure.com/wiki/Malware "Malware") / [hardware backdoor](https://www.kicksecure.com/wiki/Backdoor#Hardware_Backdoor "Backdoor")) is prevented. | |:---:|----|
Everything im doing is the normal way, go into main system to check/update. However, does that mean I cant install things from the daily use instance?
Sorry, im just trying to grasp everything about this system, please forgive me.

item.title: Can I use sudo in daily use
item.dc:creator: Patrick
item.description:
Installations that require sudo cannot be performed in a sysmaint session.

Installation or executables in the user home folder are still possible until we implement home folder noexec.

Kicksecure – 13 May 26

Enhanced Security via Mount Options and Compiler Restrictions

Upcoming security enhancements include mounting key directories with secure options and restricting compiler and interpreter access by default.

Scripts are still possible until we implement:

Whonix Forum – 19 Feb 24

lock down interpreters / compilers (interpreter lock) (compiler lock)
